report.summary: Analyzed chunk 1 of daedalus/eval/mutate.py: documented mutation generation framework with filters and operators.
risks: covered_lines | medium | Falls back to {} if coverage DB missing; caller may treat {} as 'no coverage' rather than 'unknown', diluting scores. | Add explicit documentation that {} means unknown and must be treated as such.

_is_display_constant | low | Recursively walks all ancestors, may misidentify constants in deeply nested display calls; also doesn't handle f-strings or string formatting calls like .format(). | Clarify scope or add more call patterns.

trivially_equivalent | low | Compilation is safe but compile() may raise other exceptions (e.g., MemoryError) that are not caught; also only catches trivial equivalence, not semantic. | Catch all exceptions or document the limitation.

DROP_ARGUMENT | medium | Drops first argument; may break calls where the first argument is critical and subsequent ones are optional, producing unparseable mutants. | Consider dropping a random argument or skipping calls with only one argument.

EARLY_RETURN | medium | Inserts return None after docstring; if body has multiple statements after docstring, the early return may skip important code, but the operator is still plausible. | Already documented behavior; low risk.
WEAKEN_COMPARISON | low | Only weakens first operator in chain; chained comparisons (e.g., a < b < c) are not handled. | Noted; extension possible.
todos: Add explicit handling for {} return from covered_lines to prevent misinterpretation.
Extend _is_display_constant to cover f-strings and .format() calls.
Consider catching all exceptions in trivially_equivalent for robustness.
Improve DROP_ARGUMENT to drop a random argument rather than always the first.
Consider handling chained comparisons in WEAKEN_COMPARISON.
Add more guard names to GUARD_NAMES tuple if needed.

claims.text: WHY THIS EXISTS, STATED AGAINST MY OWN RESULT ... detection rate measured on the examples that motivated it is not evidence of anything.
claims.why: The docstring explains the motivation; no code contradicts this claim.

claims.text: mechanical — AST operators applied to real functions in this repository, not hand-picked incidents
claims.why: The chunk defines operators but does not show the selection of functions or the application to repository code.

claims.text: unbounded — as many as you ask for
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the generation loop that produces multiple mutants.

claims.text: marker-free — no 'SEEDED DEFECT' comment exists
claims.why: No such comment appears in this chunk; the code does not insert markers.

claims.text: deterministic — a seed picks the sites, so a claim is reproducible.
claims.why: The _mutate_tree function takes a random.Random instance as argument, enabling deterministic behavior with a fixed seed.

claims.text: It is a plausible defect: a dropped call, an inverted condition, a changed constant, a weakened comparison.
claims.why: The operators DROP_CALL, INVERT_CONDITION, CHANGE_CONSTANT, WEAKEN_COMPARISON are defined and implemented.

claims.text: It is NOT necessarily a behaviour-changing one — some mutants are equivalent
claims.why: The function trivially_equivalent explicitly detects equivalent mutants via bytecode comparison.

claims.text: Every mutant is checked to still PARSE. A mutant that breaks syntax is not a defect
claims.why: _mutate_tree attempts ast.parse on the mutated source and returns None on SyntaxError.

claims.text: A mutant here can never be a product defect.
claims.why: SKIP_PATH_PARTS excludes paths like 'tests', '__pycache__', etc., which are not product code.

claims.text: Cosmetic or self-describing methods: a changed repr is not a defect worth catching
claims.why: SKIP_FUNCTIONS includes __repr__, __str__, __hash__, __doc__, etc.

claims.text: Constants whose value is display text, not behaviour. Changing a log message or a docstring is not a defect
claims.why: _is_display_constant function identifies constants that are arguments to display calls like print, log, etc.

claims.text: Guard vocabulary. Real incidents in the hand-written corpus were all removals of exactly this kind of code
claims.why: GUARD_NAMES contains guard-related names, and _looks_like_a_guard uses them to prioritize sites.

claims.text: A mutant on a line no test reaches is a GUARANTEED survivor: it cannot be caught by the gate, so measuring it only dilutes the score.
claims.why: The function reads coverage data to identify covered lines, and returns {} if unavailable, with a note that {} must be treated as unknown.

claims.text: This reads a coverage database if one is present and returns {} if not — and the caller must treat {} as 'unknown', never as 'nothing is covered'.
claims.why: The code returns {} when no coverage DB is found; the docstring explicitly warns the caller.

claims.text: Field-compatible with the hand-written corpus's Mutation where it matters (id, defect_class, file), so the same measurement code reads both.
claims.why: Mutant has id, defect_class, file fields; also provides find and replace properties for compatibility.

claims.text: True if the two sources compile to IDENTICAL bytecode.
claims.why: The function compiles both sources and compares fingerprints that include co_code, co_consts, etc.

claims.text: Compilation is not execution: compile() builds a code object and runs nothing, so this is safe on arbitrary repository source.
claims.why: The function uses compile() only, which does not execute the code.

claims.text: Structural fingerprint of a code object, recursing into nested ones.
claims.why: The function recurses into nested code objects via co_consts and includes co_code, co_names, etc.

claims.text: Names and constants are included because a mutant that only changes a constant DOES change behaviour; what is excluded is line-number tables and filenames, which differ for reasons that are not the program.
claims.why: The fingerprint includes co_names and co_consts (via repr), and excludes co_filename and co_lnotab implicitly.

claims.text: (exact source of the function, its lines) or None if it cannot be sliced.
claims.why: The function returns a tuple of the function source and empty string, or None if end_lineno is missing or invalid.

claims.text: Uses ast.unparse on the whole function, which normalises formatting. That is FINE for this purpose and worth stating: the measurement compares the mutant against its own unparsed original, never against the raw file, so normalisation cannot masquerade as a change.
claims.why: The function uses ast.unparse on the mutated tree, and the docstring explains the rationale.

claims.text: AFTER the docstring, never before. Inserting ahead of it demotes the docstring from body[0] to an ordinary string expression, which makes a LITERAL appear out of nowhere — an artefact of the generator that was measured suppressing detection of this operator from ~100% to 37%.
claims.why: The code strips leading docstring (Constant expression) then inserts the return after the docstring's position.

observations.what: covered_lines returns {} when no coverage database found, but the docstring warns caller to treat {} as unknown. However, the function also returns {} on error or if no coverage file exists; the caller may misinterpret.
_is_display_constant recursively walks all ancestors; may be expensive and may misidentify constants in nested display calls.
trivially_equivalent catches SyntaxError and ValueError but not other exceptions from compile (e.g., MemoryError, RecursionError).

DROP_ARGUMENT always drops the first argument (node.args[0]) but the code shows sites.append(node) and later target = rng.choice(sites); the actual dropping logic is in the next chunk. The docstring says 'a flag is lost from a call' which implies a specific argument, but the code may drop any argument. The implementation is incomplete in this chunk.
EARLY_RETURN inserts return None after docstring; if there is no docstring, it inserts at beginning of body. This may produce mutants that skip important initialization.
WEAKEN_COMPARISON only weakens the first comparison operator; chained comparisons (e.g., a < b < c) are not handled.
